source_text: Ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἀπεδείξαμεν παῖδας ἡμᾶς τοὺς πάντας ὑπὸ τῆς γραφῆς καλουμένους οὐ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς Χριστῷ κατηκολουθηκότας ἡμᾶς νηπίους ἀλληγορουμένους, μόνον δὲ εἶναι τέλειον τὸν πατέρα τῶν ὅλων (ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ ὁ πατήρ), ὥρα ἡμῖν ἑπομένοις τῇ τάξει καὶ τὸν παιδαγωγὸν ἡμῶν εἰπεῖν ὅστις ἐστί. καλεῖται δὲ Ἰησοῦς. ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε οὖν ποιμένα ἑαυτὸν καλεῖ καὶ λέγει »ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός«, κατὰ μεταφορὰν ἀπὸ τῶν ποιμένων τῶν καθηγουμένων τοῖς προβάτοις ὁ καθηγούμενος τῶν παιδίων παιδαγωγὸς νοούμενος, ὁ τῶν νηπίων κηδεμονικὸς ποιμήν· ἁπλοῖ γὰρ οἱ νήπιοι ὡς πρόβατα ἀλληγορούμενοι· »καὶ γενήσονται«, φησίν, »οἱ πάντες μία ποίμνη καὶ εἷς ποιμήν.« παιδαγωγὸς οὖν εἰκότως ὁ λόγος ὁ τοὺς παῖδας ἡμᾶς εἰς σωτηρίαν ἄγων. ἐναργέστατα γοῦν ὁ λόγος περὶ ἑαυτοῦ διὰ Ὠσηὲ εἴρηκεν »ἐγὼ δὲ παιδευτὴς ὑμῶν εἰμι«. παιδαγωγία δὲ ἡ θεοσέβεια, μάθησις οὖσα θεοῦ θεραπείας καὶ παίδευσις εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἀγωγή τε ὀρθὴ ἀνάγουσα εἰς οὐρανόν. Παιδαγωγία δε καλεῖται πολλαχῶς· καὶ γὰρ ἡ τοῦ ἀγομένου καὶ μανθάνοντος, καὶ ἡ τοῦ ἄγοντος καὶ διδάσκοντος, καὶ αὐτὴ τρίτον ἡ ἀγωγή, καὶ τὰ διδασκόμενα τέταρτον, οἷον αἱ ἐντολαί. ἔστι δὲ ἡ κατὰ τὸν θεὸν παιδαγωγία κατευθυσμὸς ἀληθείας εἰς ἐποπτείαν θεοῦ καὶ πράξεων ἁγίων ὑποτύπωσις ἐν αἰωνίῳ διαμονῇ. ὥσπερ οὖν κατευθύνει τὴν φάλαγγα ὁ στρατηγὸς τῆς σωτηρίας τῶν μισθοφόρων προμηθούμενος, καὶ ὡς ὁ κυβερνήτης οἰακίζει τὸ σκάφος σῴζειν προαιρούμενος τοὺς ἐμπλέοντας, οὕτως καὶ ὁ παιδαγωγὸς ἄγει τοὺς παῖδας ἐπὶ τὴν σωτήριον δίαιταν τῆς ἡμῶν αὐτῶν ἕνεκεν κηδεμονίας· καὶ καθόλου ὁπόσα ἂν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐλόγως αἰτήσαιμεν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι, ταῦτα πειθομένοις τῷ παιδαγωγῷ περιέσται. ὅνπερ οὖν τρόπον ὁ κυβερνήτης οὐκ αἰεὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ὑπείκει, ἀντίπρῳρος δὲ ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε ὅλαις ἀνθίσταται καταιγίσιν, οὕτως ὁ παιδαγωγὸς οὐχὶ τοῖς ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τῷδε καταπνέουσιν ἀνέμοις ὑπείκει ποτὲ οὐδὲ ἐπιτρέπει αὐτοῖς τὸ παιδίον, ὥσπερ σκάφος, εἰς θηριώδη καὶ ἀσελγῆ προσρῆξαι δίαιταν, μόνῳ δὲ ἄρα τῷ ἀληθείας πνεύματι ἔπουρος ἀρθεὶς ἀντέχεται μάλα ἐρρωμένως τῶν οἰάκων τοῦ παιδός, τῶν ὤτων λέγω, ἕως ἂν ἀβλαβὲς καθορμίσῃ τὸ παιδίον εἰς τὸν λιμένα τῶν οὐρανῶν· τὸ μὲν γὰρ πάτριον καλούμενον παρ᾿ ἀνθρώποις ἔθος ὅσον οὐδέπω παρέρχεται, ἡ δὲ ἀγωγὴ ἡ θεία κτῆμά ἐστιν εἰς ἀεὶ παραμένον.
pass_a_gloss: Since we have shown that all of us are called children, not only by scripture, but also that we who follow Christ are called infants, and that only the Father of all is perfect, for the Son is in Him and the Father is in the Son, it is time for us, following the order, to say who our Instructor is. He is called Jesus. For He sometimes calls Himself a shepherd and says 'I am the good shepherd', using a metaphor from shepherds who lead sheep, the one who leads children is considered a tutor, a guardian shepherd of infants; for infants are simple like sheep. And He says 'they will all be one flock and one shepherd'. Therefore, the Word is reasonably our Instructor, leading us children to salvation. Clearly, the Word has spoken about Himself through Hosea, saying 'I am your tutor'. Tutorship is reverence for God, being a lesson in serving God and a training for knowledge of the truth, and a straight path leading to heaven. Tutorship is called by many names: both the one being led and learning, and the one leading and teaching, and thirdly the leading itself, and fourthly the things being taught, such as commandments. But the divine tutorship is a guidance of truth for the contemplation of God and an impression of holy deeds in eternal abiding. Just as the general of the salvation of the mercenaries leads the phalanx, taking care of them, and as the helmsman steers the ship to save those on board, so also the Instructor leads the children to the salvific diet for the sake of our own guardianship; and in general, whatever we might reasonably ask from God to happen to us, these things will be around us if we obey the Instructor. For just as the helmsman does not always yield to the winds, but sometimes resists all the storms, so also the Instructor does not yield to the winds blowing in this world, nor does He permit them to dash the child, like a ship, against a savage and shameless diet, but only yields to the Spirit of truth, and having been raised, He strongly holds the child's sails, that is, the ears, until He moors the child safely in the harbor of the heavens; for the paternal custom called 'ancestral' by people is still not past, but the divine leading is a possession remaining forever.
pass_b_english: We have shown that all of us are called children not only by Scripture but also that we who follow Christ are called infants, and that only the Father of all is perfect, for the Son is in Him and the Father is in the Son. Therefore it is time for us, following the proper order, to say who our Instructor is. He is called Jesus. For He sometimes calls Himself a shepherd and says, "I am the good shepherd" (John 10:11), using a metaphor from shepherds who lead sheep: the one who leads children is considered a tutor, a guardian shepherd of infants, for infants are simple like sheep. And He says, "They will all be one flock and one shepherd" (John 10:16). The Word is therefore reasonably our Instructor, leading us children to salvation. Clearly the Word has spoken about Himself through Hosea, saying, "I am your tutor" (Hosea). Tutorship is reverence for God, being a lesson in serving God and a training for knowledge of the truth, and a straight path leading to heaven. Tutorship is called by many names: both the one being led and learning, and the one leading and teaching, and thirdly the leading itself, and fourthly the things being taught, such as commandments. But the divine tutorship is a guidance of truth for the contemplation of God and an impression of holy deeds in eternal abiding. Just as the general of the salvation of the mercenaries leads the phalanx, taking care of them, and as the helmsman steers the ship to save those on board, so also the Instructor leads the children to the salvific way of life for the sake of our own guardianship; and in general, whatever we might reasonably ask from God to happen to us, these things will surround us if we obey the Instructor. For just as the helmsman does not always yield to the winds but sometimes resists all the storms, so also the Instructor does not yield to the winds blowing in this world, nor does He permit them to dash the child, like a ship, against a savage and shameless way of life, but only yields to the Spirit of truth, and having been raised, He strongly holds the child's sails—that is, the ears—until He moors the child safely in the harbor of the heavens; for the paternal custom called 'ancestral' by people has not yet passed away, but the divine leading is a possession remaining forever.
